description: Nyx is an open-source flight dynamics tool for mission design and orbit determination, covering trajectory optimisation, orbit estimation and Monte Carlo analysis, built in Rust for speed, automation and scalability. Its README cites use on lunar missions including Firefly Blue Ghost 1 and NASA/Advanced Space CAPSTONE, with worked examples such as a James Webb Space Telescope Monte Carlo simulation and orbit determination of the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter. It covers Earth orbit and cislunar scenarios defined by the user. It is developed by Nyx Space and published as the nyx-space crate and Python package; version 2.6.0 was released on 12 September 2026. The core is under the AGPL-3.0 licence, which the README says is free for individuals, non-profits, academic institutions and companies with annual revenue up to one million US dollars, while others must release linked software under the same licence or buy a commercial licence through the pricing page. Caveats: the copyleft terms affect integration into proprietary tools, and users need Rust or Python skills. It supports hazard exposure and resilience analysis of spacecraft operations and optimisation of trajectories for space infrastructure; a related record is the Orekit space flight dynamics library.
name: Nyx spaceflight dynamics toolkit
